title: Klunk question bank
description: A set of questions, normally one file per topic. Banks live in the teacher's own folder and are never committed to this repository.

syllabusId.description: Default syllabus for questions in this file. A question may override it.

id.description: Stable within the folder. Papers reference questions by it, so changing it orphans every paper that used the question.

questionText.description: Empty only when the question is entirely its parts, which is how the 2016, 2018 and 2019 HSC papers print one: the heading is followed straight by (a). Requiring a stem there would mean inventing words the examination never printed, so the rule is text or parts, enforced by the anyOf above.

marks.description: Total for the question. The profile decides whether this must be a whole number.

syllabus.description: What this question assesses. Stable ids, not a 'Subject > Unit > Topic' path string: paths break the moment a topic is renamed, whereas an id survives it.

pointIds.description: The most precise link, e.g. 'HSC-01.07'. Coverage reporting counts these.

outcomes.description: Outcome codes, e.g. 'H1.1'. Held on the question because not every syllabus maps outcomes to content points.

stimulus.description: Images, diagrams or source material shown with the question. Design and Technology leans on product photographs and sketches far more than a text subject does, so this is first-class rather than an afterthought.

markingGuide.description: Everything that appears in the marking guide and never on the student paper.

criteria.description: Mark-by-mark or band criteria for the question as a whole. A question split into parts carries its criteria on the parts instead.

answersCouldInclude.description: What a marker should accept, one point per entry. Every question in a NESA marking guideline ends with an 'Answers could include:' list, and it is the longest part of it: 2025 HSC Visual Arts Question 3 runs to twelve points. Distinct from 'notes', which is an aside about how to mark, where this is the substance being marked against.

source.description: Where the question came from. Extracted past-paper questions must carry this: reusing a recent HSC question in a school trial is a real hazard, and Klunk can only warn about it if the provenance is recorded.

origin.description: 'adapted' means derived from a past paper but reworded.

copyright.description: Who owns it. An extracted NESA question is NESA's, which constrains where the paper containing it may go.

config.description: Type-specific settings. See the per-type definitions below.

criterion.description: One row of a marking guide's criteria table.

marks.description: The mark, or the bottom of the band where 'marksTo' is present.

marksTo.description: The top of a band, so '13-15' is marks 13 and marksTo 15. Every HSC extended response is banded, and from 2018 a six-mark short answer carries a band too, so this is the normal case rather than an exotic one. Without it a marking guide prints a single number where the examination printed a range, which is wrong on the page a marker reads.

description.description: What a response in this band does. A NESA band is two or three separate points rather than one sentence, so newlines separate them and the marking guide prints them as the bulleted list the guidelines print.

file.description: Path relative to the bank file. Kept as a path rather than embedded base64 so the folder stays diffable and an image can be replaced without editing JSON.

alt.description: Required for images if the paper is ever read by a screen reader.

align.description: Where an image sits across the text column. Absent means centre, which is what the examinations do, so the default is never written down. Ignored on a text stimulus, which prints as a block quote.

maxHeightMm.description: Printed height cap. A tall diagram shrinks to an unreadable width on A4, so landscape is usually right.

feedback.description: Why this distractor is tempting. Should name the specific misconception, not say 'incorrect'.

shuffle.description: Shuffled deterministically per question, so option letters stay identical between the student paper and the marking guide across rebuilds.

multipleResponseConfig.description: One stem, a lettered list, and more than one right answer. Printed by the Enterprise Computing Year 11 papers over questions 10-12 in both 2024 and 2025, under the rubric 'place an X next to each alternative that answers the question. (Multiple items may be selected)'. Six or seven options in every instance, and the paper never prints how many are correct.

choices.description: Three at least: with two, a question with one right answer is multiple choice and one with two right answers asks nothing.

feedback.description: Why this option is or is not one of the answers.

correctAnswers.description: Zero-based indices into choices, in any order. Deliberately NOT required, unlike multipleChoiceConfig's 'correctAnswer': a question paper transcribed without its markscheme does not state the answer, and the alternative is inventing one. That is exactly what #64 caught doing silently. Absent means unknown and Klunk says so; it never stands for 'none'.

shuffle.description: As for multiple choice: deterministic per question, so the letters agree between the student paper and the marking guide.

matchingConfig.description: Two lists, drawn together. The Enterprise Computing Year 11 papers print questions 13-15 this way in both 2024 and 2025: a numbered column, a lettered column beside it, and 'draw lines linking items on the left with matching items on the right'. Not a table question, because the right-hand column is a closed list the student chooses from rather than cells they fill in.

items.description: The left column, numbered 1, 2, 3 in the order given.

matches.description: Zero-based indices into options. An array rather than a single index because the 2024 paper's own rubric says '(Multiple lines can start and end from any item)'. Every question in both years happens to be one-to-one, but the examination does not promise it, so the model does not either. Absent means the answer is not recorded, for the reason multipleResponseConfig's correctAnswers gives.

options.description: The right column, lettered A, B, C after shuffling. May be longer than 'items', which leaves spare options nothing links to.

shuffle.description: Shuffles the lettered column only. The numbered column is the teacher's own order and carries the question's sense; the letters are what would otherwise run 1-A, 2-B, 3-C and answer the question for the student.

answerLines.description: Ruled lines on the student paper. Omit to let the profile derive it from the marks.

parts.description: Sub-parts (a), (b), (c). Their marks must sum to the question's total.

criteria.description: A NESA marking guide marks part by part, under its own 'Question 11 (a)' heading. Flattening those into the question's own criteria loses which part each one belongs to, and then the printed guide puts them in the wrong place.

stimulus.description: Images or source material this part alone refers to, printed between what the part asks and its answer space. The 2025 HSC Biology paper prints Question 28 with one picture before part (a), one inside (a) and one inside (b), which a question-level list cannot express. On the part rather than a pointer from the stimulus to a label, for the reason criteria are: a label reference can dangle and nothing here can check it.

spaceMm.description: Width and height of the blank drawing area on the printed page.

grid.description: Print a faint grid in the drawing area.

cells.description: One entry per answer column, in order, so a row with columns [Material, Property, Use] carries two: the Property cell and the Use cell. The first column holds the row label and is not a cell.

answers.description: Every wording a marker should accept in this one cell, listed separately.

blankCells.description: Whether cells print empty for the student to complete.
